It's very true. The HP culture was very favorable towards the people who made the company great. Then, at the height of the merger and the market collapses, she comes along and executes the first ever mandatory layoff at HP in it's history. My brother worked there for more than a decade before she came to the helm. He was a senior system's architect, responsible for several internal systems used at multiple levels of upper management throughout the company, and his development team consisted of dozens of SMEs across the globe. As a result of this, he worked from home 5 days a week, and had widely flexible hours in order to meet with his various staff members several times a week. Some days he was up at 3AM for conference calls, others he was starting late and working till 10PM.

After she took the head office, she quickly killed the work-from-home plan for the majority of the company, and left no exemptions in place for personnel who had unique scenarios such as my brother. As a result, he had to work the standard 8-5 in the office, and his employees were forced to do the same locally in all of their regional facilities. Her reasoning was that working in the office fostered communication and teamwork, but given that not a single person on his team was even in the country, much less his office, this was a pointless and destructive change that had a zero-tolerance exception system attached to it.

The result was that he could no longer communicate with several subordinates in a normal fashion, and he had to result to off-hours calls and chats to resolve this. They, like him, had to drive to their nearest HP office, some of which were hours away, and sit at a cubicle by themselves, just to do the same work they were doing from their home office prior. Most of his team quit within six months. He was gone within a year, and within two, the entire original staff of the SME layer of his department, which was cross-platform internal tools and development, had also left. Most of these people were senior engineers and experts, recognized for their skills and results.
